title: Testing APIs
description: Learn how to write reliable tests for Next.js Route Handlers and API Routes so you can ship changes with confidence and catch regressions before users do.

data.text: Testing APIs means more than checking that a route returns 200. You need to verify that valid input succeeds, invalid input fails with the right error, and authentication works as expected. Good tests become documentation and a safety net for refactoring.

Unit tests check one function in isolation, mocking everything around it. Integration tests call the actual HTTP layer with a real or in-memory database so the full request-to-response path is exercised. For APIs, integration tests give you the most confidence.

items: Unit tests: fast, isolated, good for complex validation logic
Integration tests: slower, more realistic, catch routing and serialization bugs
Use a test database or transaction rollbacks to keep tests clean
Run integration tests in CI on every pull request

data.text: Vitest is a fast test runner compatible with Vite-based projects like Next.js. To test a Route Handler, import the exported function directly and pass it a mock `Request` object. This keeps tests fast and avoids starting a real server.

data.title: Unit testing a GET Route Handler

data.text: When testing mutations, send an invalid body and assert that you get a 400 with the expected validation issues. This proves your validator is wired correctly and your error formatter works.

data.title: Testing validation failure in a POST handler

data.text: Integration Testing with a Real Database

For deeper confidence, run tests against a real database. Use a dedicated test database URL, run migrations before the suite, and wrap each test in a transaction that you roll back so one test never affects another.

data.title: Vitest setup with database transaction rollback
Test Behavior, Not Implementation
data.text: Assert on the HTTP status, response body, and database state. Avoid peeking into private variables or mocking internal helpers. If you refactor the handler later, behavior-based tests keep passing.

Configure your CI pipeline to run tests on every pull request. Use a separate test database, set `NODE_ENV=test`, and fail the build if any test breaks. This catches regressions before they reach production.

data.title: Key Takeaways
items: Unit test handlers by importing them and passing mock Request objects
Test both success paths and validation/authentication failures
Use integration tests with a real database for critical flows
Run tests in CI on every pull request to catch regressions early
